knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A sticky patch contaminates the head. The learner stops, removes the matter and fits a clean head. Continuing or dampening the head spreads the residue.
The required pattern is edges first, then figure-of-eight passes from the far point back toward the exit. Random strokes and straight lines are not the method.
Mop heads are stored head up in a holder. Heads stored face down collect dirt and dust.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied vacuum, the learner reads the test label and checks the plug, flex, bag and filter, and states whether the vacuum may be used.
On a supplied floor area with a planted chewing gum patch, the learner removes the gum before sweeping and fits a clean head, observed by the assessor.
The learner sweeps a supplied area edges first, then in figure-of-eight passes from the far point toward the exit, with the mop head kept in contact with the floor throughout.
The learner stores the mop head head up and the dust pan in its colour group at the end of the task.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks (three questions, so all three must be correct to reach 80%; flagged for review). Practical sign-off is separate: the assessor signs off each practical criterion as observed.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
Pre-use check record for the vacuum
Photo of the swept area, where the site permits
stopWorkCriteria: Learner uses a vacuum with a damaged flex, bare wire or expired test label
Learner sweeps over chewing gum or a sticky patch without removing it
Learner sweeps a wet floor as though it were dry
Learner creates a dust cloud and does not stop to correct the method
